مُطَارٌ Made to fly away: En-Nábighah says, “وَلِرَهْطِ حَرَّابٍ وَقَدٍّ سُورَةٌ
فِى المَجْدِ لَيْسَ غُرَابُهُ بِمُطَارِ
” [And to the family of Harráb and Kadd belongs an eminence in glory of which they fear not any diminution: lit., of which the crow is not made to fly away; the greatness of their glory being likened to abundant seed-produce, as has been shown above: see 2]: (S:) A 'Obeyd says that Harráb and Kadd were two men of the BenooAsad. (TA in art. قد.) ―
-b2- See also طَيَّارٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
